business_problem: Leishen Intelligence needed to reduce the cost and deployment friction of autonomous forklifts while making multi-vehicle coordination, perception, and warehouse management practical for real customers.
solution_summary: Leishen Intelligence worked with Huawei Cloud to industrialize 3D SLAM forklift and AGV solutions for warehouse logistics. On the edge and control side, Huawei Atlas acts as the core compute unit running Leishen's 3D SLAM lidar navigation, motion-control, pallet-recognition, and 3D protection algorithms so forklifts can steer, brake, load, and unload autonomously. A Huawei cloud scheduling layer then coordinates multiple vehicle types, assigning jobs and planning routes in real time across shared maps. ECS adds centralized data processing and remote management so the company can move beyond isolated edge devices and build reusable intelligent management systems around the vehicles. Additional integration through LDM and information platforms exposes standard APIs to WMS, WCS, FMS, and smart location-monitoring systems. The overall design links on-vehicle perception and control with cloud dispatch and enterprise software for multi-vehicle autonomous logistics.

"The informatization platform improved solution response rate by 40% and integrates with WMS, WCS, FMS, and smart storage-location monitoring. (original: 基于华为云智能制造LDM及信息化平台，助力镭神智能业务开发效率，系统方案响应率提升40%，打通整场设备流、信息流，标准的API接口可兼容多种系统软件，同时支持配套WMS、WCS、FMS、智能库位监测系统。)"
data_flow: Atlas-based vehicles capture lidar and task data on the forklift, where 3D SLAM and control algorithms generate local decisions. Task state and fleet data are then sent to the cloud scheduling system and ECS-backed services, which coordinate routes and expose results to warehouse-management platforms.
